title: Arriving in Chicago and joining Local 208
summary: He joined Local 208 soon after its charter, discusses past presidents, serves as vice president and leads a concert orchestra for the Music Performance Trust Fund.

bands.name: Music Performance Trust Fund concert orchestra

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: I was just about, yes, just about 23. When I came here, uh, this local, 208, had just been given a charter. That- the July of that year. Mm-hmm. And, uh, this picture you see up there- Oh, yeah. Is a picture of all of the presidents. The man in the upper left-hand corner was the first president. His name was Alexander Armand, originated from New Orleans himself.
And I became a member here under his administration and have been ever since. These are all the presidents we've had up to the present, Mr. Gray, you see in the center there.

Mm-hmm. Now, Smith, Smith is gone. Uh, both of the Smiths are gone. The upper one, Ed Smith, and George Smith is gone. The one at the bottom there, Verona Biggs, he's gone. And Swan, up to the right-hand corner, he's gone. Is the Mr. Swift still around? Now, uh, Stewart is still here. Uh, Swift is still here. Dr. Giles is still here, and Mr. Gray.
But all of these- the other persons practically retired from the music game.
You were almost a charter member of the union here.
Well, uh, I came immediately after they got that charter, so I couldn't say that I was a charter member. No, almost. Because- but I was among the first members during the organizations. Yeah.
Uh, how long have you been an officer of the union? Oh, my dear. Ever since I can remember, but that's not so long.

Yes, I've been an officer most of the time. Even from the very first time I came here. In some capacity, but I've been vice president, I guess, about 20 years now. Maybe longer. I have never had any desire for the presidency, because I never felt I wanted to give up my music activities. Which I would have to do if I was at the head of the organization. As it is, I stay in the background as its vice president, and I- I can still function as a musician.
That's wonderful. I think that you have that interest in music, because a lot of people that have been in the business that long may-

No, and I still- and I still do it, because I am now- I have a concert orchestra that's working on the Music Performance Trust Fund, and we give free concerts around schools and hospitals. And I'm getting a tremendous kick out of that work.
